title: CFA-01 World / Ontology / Context — Peer Relationship & Distance Map
purpose: A machine-readable map of how CFA-01 relates to the Architecture Steward and the other registered Core Function Areas: what CFA-01 needs from each peer, what the peer is likely to need from CFA-01, where the semantic/operational seams are close, and where boundary collision is most likely.

epistemic_notice.peer_roles: Observed from the repository roster and peer bootstrap/identity documents.
epistemic_notice.relationship_scores: CFA-01's own derived assessment, not a peer-authored claim.
epistemic_notice.peer_likely_need: Derived inference from current peer mission/boundary documents; not peer agreement and should be confirmed through Commons dialogue.
epistemic_notice.distance: Analytical aid only; not a maturity, priority, quality, or authority score.
epistemic_notice.score_model_v2: Operational distance is CFA-01's own analytical instrument. It is not a maturity, priority, quality, authority, or personnel ranking.

relationship_classes: The Steward provides the map/reconciliation machinery through which CFA-01's meaning becomes development-legible.
Peer owns durable representation/identity mechanics while CFA-01 supplies what the represented thing means.
Peer preserves meaning continuity across another semantic chain; CFA-01 supplies World/Thing/Context references that ground it.
Peer decides permission semantics; CFA-01 supplies the world objects/effects that authority acts upon without becoming permission.
Peer turns intent into Work/execution; CFA-01 supplies addressable world targets, context, and semantic effects.
Peer realizes capabilities against external providers/resources; CFA-01 defines the world-facing semantic targets and their context.
Peer assembles pieces; CFA-01 defines the world/context in which those pieces are meaningful and connected.
Peer renders/manipulates experience; CFA-01 owns the canonical semantics being represented, not the representation.
Peer changes the system; CFA-01 identifies which world meanings, identities, relationships, and contexts must survive change.
Peer enforces irreducible runtime guarantees; CFA-01 supplies semantics but must not smuggle domain ontology into K0.

definitions.semantic_overlap: 0 = largely disjoint concepts; 10 = same conceptual substrate.
definitions.causal_dependency: 0 = CFA-01 can close its work independently; 10 = closure repeatedly depends on peer semantics/contracts.
definitions.handoff_density: 0 = rare reference; 10 = recurring negotiated exchange is expected.
definitions.shared_vocabulary: 0 = little shared terminology; 10 = substantial common vocabulary.
definitions.peer_evidence_value: 0 = peer output is peripheral; 10 = peer output is a critical basis for CFA-01 work.
definitions.peer_likely_need: 0 = peer can normally proceed without CFA-01; 10 = peer likely requires CFA-01 semantic outputs to stay coherent.
definitions.replacement_sensitivity: 0 = peer changes rarely affect World semantics; 10 = peer evolution can materially change World meaning or continuity.
definitions.boundary_collision_risk: 0 = crisp seam; 10 = strong temptation to duplicate ownership.

distance_formula.proximity_index: weighted average of semantic_overlap, causal_dependency, handoff_density, shared_vocabulary, peer_evidence_value, peer_likely_need, replacement_sensitivity

bands.0-20: IMMEDIATE — daily/structural neighbor; shared boundary must stay explicit.
bands.21-35: NEAR — strong recurring seam; handoffs should be designed, not improvised.
bands.36-50: CONNECTED — meaningful dependency, but different core questions.
bands.51-65: DISTANT — indirect dependency; coordination mostly through contracts/views.
bands.66-100: REMOTE — weak direct coupling; avoid forcing a relationship.

architecture-steward.role: Architectural memory, documentation integrity, reconciliation and coordination
what_i_need_from_peer: A current architecture graph and ownership/reconciliation model.
Explicit status/freshness/lineage machinery so World claims are mapped without becoming graph authority.
A place to surface cross-agent dependencies, contradictions and boundary changes.
what_peer_likely_needs_from_me: World/ontology responsibility nodes and semantically meaningful edges.
Clear distinctions among canonical World meaning, projection, Context, Space, Address and Relationship.
Material changes in World semantics, ownership or open questions that should trigger graph repull.
architecture-steward.authority_boundary: Steward owns architecture mapping/reconciliation; CFA-01 owns World-domain meaning within its ratified scope.

what_i_need_from_peer: Canonical record/persistence boundaries for Things, Relationships, identity assertions, lifecycle state and World-relevant data.
Stable identity/revision semantics that let a World meaning survive storage evolution.
A strict distinction between semantic object meaning and storage representation.
what_peer_likely_needs_from_me: Semantic type/relationship definitions that tell persistence what a record means.
Lifecycle semantics for objects and relationships, including tombstone/history distinctions.
Rules for which World concepts are canonical records versus projections/context.
data-model.authority_boundary: CFA-02 owns canonical data representation/identity/persistence mechanics; CFA-01 owns meaning of World objects/relationships.

semantic-continuity.role: Semantic continuity across self-knowledge, language, command, intent, execution meaning, evidence and representation
what_i_need_from_peer: Cross-plane semantic tracing so World terms retain meaning as they move into grounding, Intent, Work, Evidence and representation.
A challenge mechanism for terminology collisions and false equivalence between representation and canonical World meaning.
A maintained semantic crosswalk rather than a second ontology.
what_peer_likely_needs_from_me: Canonical World references for grounding natural-language commands.
Context semantics and addressability so semantic interpretation can point to actual Things/Spaces/Relationships.
Clear separation between a World fact, a projection of it, and an interpreted command about it.
semantic-continuity.authority_boundary: CFA-03 stewards continuity across planes; CFA-01 owns World-domain semantics.

what_i_need_from_peer: A hard separation between what exists/is targeted in the World and what is permitted to be done to it.
Authority-facing semantics for principal, requested effect, scope and risk.
Rules preventing a World assertion from being mistaken for permission.
what_peer_likely_needs_from_me: Semantically precise effect targets: which Thing/Relationship/Resource is being acted upon.
World scope and context needed to interpret authority boundaries.
Identity/correspondence meaning for resolving the object or principal being referenced without owning identity storage.
handoff_artifacts: world-state observations that do not imply authority
authority-governance.authority_boundary: CFA-04 owns authorization semantics; CFA-01 must never infer permission from existence, relationship, intent, or evidence.

what_i_need_from_peer: A clear model of how Work/Outcome/execution mutations become changes to World without collapsing Work into World.
Attribution and recovery semantics that let World reflect what actually happened versus what was intended.
A durable handoff for unknown external effects and reconciliation.
what_peer_likely_needs_from_me: Addressable World targets and typed object/relationship semantics.
Context relevant to a Work instance.
Rules for distinguishing intended World change, observed change, projection and unresolved state.
agency-work-execution.authority_boundary: CFA-05 owns Work/execution semantics; CFA-01 owns the meaning of resulting World state.

what_i_need_from_peer: A stable statement of what external capability/realization boundaries are visible to the World.
Separation among provider, account, session and external resource so World objects are not polluted by realization mechanics.
Knowledge of which provider-side identities are merely correspondences, not VIVIM identity.
what_peer_likely_needs_from_me: World entities/resources that a capability is intended to address.
Context needed to choose the right realization or route.
Semantic consequences of external actions, independent of browser/provider mechanics.
capability-provider-realization.authority_boundary: CFA-06 owns capability/provider/realization semantics; CFA-01 owns what those realizations act upon in the World.

what_i_need_from_peer: A way to represent compositions/plugins as meaningful parts of the environment without making the World an implementation registry.
Clarity on which plugin/composition objects are World things versus runtime mechanics.
Boundaries that stop compositions from silently becoming ontology or persistence authority.
what_peer_likely_needs_from_me: World meaning for objects/capabilities a composition assembles.
Semantic context for where a composition is useful and which Things/Spaces it touches.
Object/relationship identity semantics that keep first-party and user-created pieces addressable in the same environment.
composition-plugin-forge.authority_boundary: CFA-07 owns composition/plugin/Forge semantics; CFA-01 owns the World-domain meaning in which compositions participate.

what_i_need_from_peer: A strict projection boundary so surface/canvas/layout never becomes canonical World state.
Experience semantics for attention, focus, Space, Address and representation that do not rewrite World meaning.
A way to express uncertainty/unknown/conflict in user-facing representations without fabricating certainty.
what_peer_likely_needs_from_me: Canonical World objects/relationships/spaces to represent.
Addressability semantics for direct manipulation and navigation.
Rules for when a surface change means World mutation versus merely changing presentation.
experience-interaction-surfaces.authority_boundary: CFA-08 owns experience/surface realization; CFA-01 owns canonical World meaning.

what_i_need_from_peer: Compatibility/evolution semantics for object identity, relationships, context definitions and world projections.
Migration/replacement rules that preserve World meaning even when implementations change.
A place to express when an evolution event changes semantics versus only representation/storage.
what_peer_likely_needs_from_me: A precise statement of what must remain semantically stable through change.
Identity/correspondence invariants and relationship history that evolution cannot silently break.
World/Context impact boundaries for migration, replacement, repair and retirement.
evolution-compatibility-self-maintenance.primary_seam: semantic continuity of World ↔ system evolution
evolution-compatibility-self-maintenance.authority_boundary: CFA-09 owns evolution/compatibility/self-maintenance; CFA-01 owns World semantics and survival invariants.

what_i_need_from_peer: Knowable runtime guarantees and limits: context assembly, identity/revision/event substrate, admission, isolation, activation/recovery, without having to redefine World ontology inside K0.
Clear seams showing which World semantics are data/contract versus constitutional runtime mechanism.
what_peer_likely_needs_from_me: Domain-neutral semantic boundaries that tell K0 what it must not assume.
A clear distinction between World-domain meaning and runtime substrate concepts.
Context semantics that K0 can treat opaquely except where a contract explicitly requires it.
handoff_artifacts: K0/K1 placement disputes involving World concepts
runtime-constitution-core-substrate.authority_boundary: CFA-10 owns irreducible runtime guarantees; CFA-01 owns World semantics and must resist ontology leaking into K0.

operating_implications.default_direction: CFA-01 should behave as a semantic source/consumer at explicit seams, not as a hub that owns neighboring mechanics.
operating_implications.anti_pattern: When a peer asks CFA-01 for a generic registry, store, graph, permission flag, UI model, or runtime singleton, first test whether the request is actually a neighboring concern dressed in World terminology.
operating_implications.peer_dialogue_priority: Confirm the inferred peer_need scores through Commons or direct bootstrap dialogue before turning any inference into a durable contract.
operating_implications.distance_interpretation: High closeness means more frequent semantic coordination, not shared ownership.

relationship_model_v2.intent: Model the relationship as a multi-axis operating dependency rather than one scalar. The scalar distance is only a navigation aid.

codes.MNG: meaning dependency — peer helps determine or preserve what a World concept means
codes.CTX: context dependency — peer needs bounded World state/context
codes.DUR: durability dependency — peer consumes or produces information that must survive
codes.EXT: externalization dependency — peer maps World meaning to external systems
codes.ACT: action dependency — peer turns World meaning into authorized/executed change
codes.PRJ: projection dependency — peer presents/manipulates World representations
codes.EVO: evolution dependency — peer changes/replaces semantics or their carriers
codes.SUB: substrate dependency — peer mechanically constrains where World semantics can live
codes.MAP: meta-map dependency — Steward maps/reconciles World meaning across the repository

dimensions.semantic_proximity_0_5: How close the peer's core semantic subject is to World/Ontology/Context.
dimensions.input_dependency_0_5: How much CFA-01 needs the peer's outputs to complete its own work.
dimensions.peer_input_dependency_0_5: How much the peer needs CFA-01 outputs to complete its own work.
dimensions.boundary_collision_0_5: How easily ownership can be accidentally duplicated or conflated at this seam.
dimensions.interaction_frequency_0_5: Expected operational frequency of meaningful interaction.
dimensions.consequence_0_5: Impact of a wrong seam model on durable meaning, authority, execution, or external truth.
dimensions.transform_coupling_0_5: How often information crosses the seam in semantically consequential transformations.
dimensions.evolution_coupling_0_5: How strongly changes on one side force re-evaluation on the other.

default_channels.P0: direct peer + Architecture Steward; Commons DIRECT or focused ROOM when a sustained corridor exists
default_channels.P1: direct peer; Commons PUBLIC when broadly reusable
default_channels.P2: normal Commons/public artifact for contract clarification

decision_rules_v2: High proximity does not mean shared ownership.
High boundary collision means guard the seam more carefully; it does not mean the peer is an inappropriate owner.
A peer becomes an operational supplier when it provides evidence/contract/state CFA-01 cannot establish itself.
A peer becomes an operational customer when its correct operation depends on semantic World/Context outputs.
A notification is warranted by boundary pressure or semantic consequence, not by mere topical similarity.

World meaning is the default CFA-01 contribution; representation, storage, permission, execution, realization, composition, surface and substrate mechanics remain peer-owned unless explicit evidence changes the boundary.
When a peer requests a registry/store/graph/cache, first test whether the request is actually asking CFA-01 to absorb a neighboring responsibility.
When a peer's output changes what a Thing is, what relationship means, or what context contains, re-open the relevant World boundary even if the implementation appears local.
